title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
description: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates pros
body: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.A crash axe is usually kept ​in the cockpit in case of emergencies.The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife.The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this.While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew "Kill me, kill me!"The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidal… It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane."He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.He also said investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday."I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said.About two and half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport it begun to plunge sharply. The plane signalled a "general emergency" code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting "unlawful interference", or hijacking.In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong.Almog Itali said: "Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down."People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said.Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit. Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men - Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan - entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries. Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister's office, that the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there," he said.In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had "managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster".

schema.headline: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says

title: Burnham scraps controversial plans to curb jury trials
description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has scrapped controversial plans to curb some jury trials.Sir Keir Starmer's government had introduced proposals to allow
body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has scrapped controversial plans to curb some jury trials.Sir Keir Starmer's government had introduced proposals to allow judges to make the sole decision on cases that would lead to a sentence of less than three years.The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said only complex fraud and financial offences would be judge-alone - and it proposes that thousands of medium-level crimes should stay with volunteer magistrates, who sit without a jury.Justice Secretary Alex Norris said he had changed course came after hearing the "strength of feeling". Criminal lawyers have welcomed the decision and the Conservatives say it is a "major victory" for those who fought to defend trial by jury.Former Justice Secretary David Lammy first announced the plans in December following a recommendation in a major review of the court system in England and Wales.The series of radical reforms, including scaling back jury trials, were presented as the best way of turning around record backlogs which, in turn, were exacerbating the prison population crisis. The backlog - which has led to record delays for defendants and victims - currently stands at nearly 81,000 cases - having rocketed largely thanks to cuts before the pandemic and court closures during the national lockdowns. Official projections have estimated it could reach 100,000 before the next general election and, in a worst case scenario, climb to double that number by 2035. There are, however, indications the backlog is now stabilising after the government committed unlimited funding to pay for more judges to sit in courts that were otherwise being unused. Under the original plans, Lammy had wanted to reserve jury trials for the most serious "indictable" offences - meaning cases that are always sent to Crown Court, including murder and rape. Less serious offences, where the sentence would be no more than three years, would be decided without a jury in the Crown Court by a judge alone. Even less serious offences would stay in magistrates' courts, abolishing defendants' right to ask for a trial by jury when they feel that is their best chance of beig cleared.The proposals triggered an outcry across many parts of the criminal justice world, with many opponents saying that eroding the 800-year-old right to trial by jury would not solve the backlogs.  Andrew Thomas KC - chairman of the Criminal Bar Association, which represents barristers who work in crown and magistrates courts - said the profession was "delighted". "Justice needs juries," he said. "Nothing inspires more public trust than 12 ordinary citizens from all walks of life deciding the facts of a case together."We are also pleased that the government is going ahead with important changes in the bill to protect victims and witnesses at trial. These include new powers to prevent unfair questioning about a complainant's behaviour and to support witnesses to give their best evidence."But Thomas warned that plans to keep more middle-ranking cases before magistrates by abolishing defendants' rights to ask for a jury trial could backfire - not least because of a shortage of magistrates. "The proposal to strip defendants of their right to elect a crown court trial, combined with doubling magistrates' sentencing powers to two years, would shift 25,000 cases a year - including 5,500 jury trials - out of the crown court," he said."These are not minor offences. It includes serious and sensitive cases including assaults, sexual assaults, child abuse and grievous bodily harm. Our volunteer magistrates do an excellent job but they are completely unequipped to try complex, multi-day trials."It would be a car crash if they tried to do it, especially at this time."Barrister Karl Turner, a Labour MP who was suspended from the parliamentary party after he criticised the government's plans to reform jury trials, thanked Burnham "for his support during my campaign".Shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy said: "This is a major victory for everyone who fought to defend trial by jury, and Conservatives led that fight from day one. Labour have been forced to abandon its central attack on jury trials in the Crown Court."

schema.headline: Burnham scraps controversial plans to curb jury trials

title: Man shot dead in East Acton as people gather for memorial service
description: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including childre
body: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including children – gathered for a memorial service in west London.The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence."We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated."We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw". He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media."However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook,, external X,, external and Instagram., external Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk

title: Conservatives pledge to scrap £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge'
description: The Conservatives have promised to scrap the "absurd cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £
body: The Conservatives have promised to scrap the "absurd cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £100,000 a year.Under the current system, only families where no parent earns more than this threshold are eligible for government-funded or tax-free childcare."What we want to see is that people who work harder don't get punished for doing so," Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme.The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.The party said the move would be a "first step" in broader efforts to address issues in the tax system which damage incentives to work or invest.This will be a theme of shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith's conference speech on Monday.Since September 2025, working parents in England have been entitled to 30 hours of free childcare, external for children aged between nine months and four years old.However, to qualify both parents must earn less than £100,000 a year.The same £100,000 threshold applies to the government's tax-free childcare scheme, external.For every £8 paid into an online childcare account, the government adds £2, up to £2,000 per child per year, which parents can then use to pay for childcare.The Tories said that if they return to power they would remove the £100,000 threshold entirely so parents no longer lose childcare support when their income exceeds this level.The threshold has been criticised by economists, who point out it can leave parents worse off overall even after a pay rise of tens of thousands of pounds.Badenoch told the BBC the party didn't want "people to stop working because of that".Speaking before the party's conference, she added: "What we want to see is more people in work and not taking the wrong decisions or the wrong choices, and it doesn't matter whether they're earning £10,000 or £100,000 - what matters is that people are out there working".Asked if this could result in someone who earns £1 million a year get free childcare under a Conservative government, Badenoch responded: "It doesn't matter what you earn - we don't want you to be punished for working hard. What we're trying to do is grow our economy."The Tories argue the threshold may mean some people may delay having children until their incomes change, or decide not to start a family at all, describing scrapping it as "both pro-family and pro-growth".By providing an increased incentive to work, the Tories said the move would also boost economic growth.They added that it would tackle the "unfairness" that the threshold is calculated on an individual earner's income rather then for the whole household.In a statement, Griffith said: "Removing this childcare cliff edge is the first step in our mission to deliver lower, simpler, and fairer taxes across the board."The party said the policy would be funded by cutting the number of public servants working in "executive non-departmental public bodies" - organisations which have a role in the processes of national government but operate at arm's length from ministers, such as Arts Council England and the Environment Agency.It said this would save £1.6bn by 2029-30, covering the estimated £700 million cost of removing the childcare "cliff edge".Badenoch arrived in Birmingham on Saturday ahead of the annual conference, and vowed the party was new and different from the one that lost the 2024 general election.The party - which is currently polling behind Labour and Reform UK - is expected to use the event to lay out more of its growing policy agenda ahead of the next general election.

schema.headline: Conservatives pledge to scrap £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge'

title: The Celebrity Traitors connections that might surprise you, from Jerry Hall and Richard E Grant to Rob and Romesh
description: Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC Creative/PA WireByNoor NanjiCulture correspondentSpoiler warning: This article reveals details from
body: Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC Creative/PA WireByNoor NanjiCulture correspondentSpoiler warning: This article reveals details from the first two episodes of The Celebrity Traitors"I know Rob very, very well. I mean, I've sat next to him as he's had a colonic."That was Romesh Ranganathan, reminding us - in case we were in any doubt - of his close friendship with Rob Beckett in the opening episode of The Celebrity Traitors.His words sum up the key difference between this series and the regular civilian version. In Celebrity Traitors, the players aren't just on-screen competitors - many actually know each other outside the show.Lots have worked together, and some are even friends. And those previous connections can have a huge impact on the show's dynamics.It's also partly why it is quite so delightful to watch - as friendships unravel, and former co-stars turn on each other.We've been unpicking the six degrees of separation. Here are some of the connections we've found - if you spot any more, we'd love to know. Get in touch with your thoughts in the comments section below.The Rob and Romesh bromanceThe dynamic between Rob Beckett and Romesh Ranganathan is one of the most enjoyable to watch play out this year.As well as being great friends in real life, they have also worked together repeatedly, including in their travel show, Rob & Romesh Vs.They've also frequently made joint appearances on panel shows such as Mock the Week.But their friendship could count for nothing in the castle, Ranganathan said ahead of the show.Image source, Joe Maher/Getty ImagesJoe and James are also friends (for now)Joe Lycett has said publicly that he's friends with James Acaster, and the pair have a running joke about how everyone gets them confused (Lycett cleared that up here, external). They’ve also worked together on the TV show Travel Man.Lycett is also friends with Joanne McNally, external - he's described her as "one of my favourite people in the world".But those loyalties could be about to be tested, especially now that Acaster has been recruited as a traitor (anyone remember how things panned out for "good friends" Alan Carr and Paloma Faith...?).Lots of them are on the comedy circuitThere are SO many comedians in this year's series.And they are all likely to know each other. In addition to the alliances above, Joe Lycett was on the TV show Last One Laughing with Rob Beckett.Joanne McNally and Romesh Ranganathan appeared on game show Unacceptable together, and James Acaster went on Ranganathan's hip hop podcast.Speaking ahead of the show, McNally insisted she and her fellow comedians "haven't been in cahoots at all"."We know that we're more than willing to throw each other under the bus," she said.As for Acaster, he's admitted the other comedians are his “biggest threat” when it comes to being detected as a traitor.“Romesh, Joe, Rob know me really well. They all know that I don’t change my mind overnight,” he said, as he pondered whether to turn and help fellow traitor Richard E Grant clear his name.Maya has rubbed shoulders with several of the starsIt won’t surprise you that the two broadcasters of the group - Maya Jama and Amol Rajan - have met their fair share of the other stars before.Rajan had previously hosted both Michael Sheen and Joe Lycett on the Radio 2 Breakfast show, and also interviewed Romesh Ranganathan on BBC Asian Network.He's also been joined on the One Show on separate occasions by Ross Kemp, Miranda Hart and James Blunt - and earlier this year, he discussed AI on stage with Hannah Fry.But in the end, Rajan became the first player to be murdered, before we really got to see the impact of those past connections.Image source, Daniele Venturelli/WireImageImage caption, Leigh-Anne Pinnock and Maya Jama were pictured together on the front row during Milan Fashion Week in 2024Meanwhile, Maya Jama is best known for hosting Love Island, but she's also popped up in loads of other places - including at this year's Brit Awards, where she presented an award with James Blunt.She's also been on Ranganathan's hip hop podcast, attended Milan Fashion Week with Leigh-Anne Pinnock, and she, Joe Lycett and James Acaster all appeared on The Big Fat Quiz of the Year.But Jama played down her connections on Celebrity Traitors, saying ahead of the show: “I've met a few people in the cast, but nobody really knows me, so we're all starting from scratch.”Bella and Sebastian are Westeros alumniUsually the younger celebs in the castle tend to know fewer people, but Bella Ramsey is pretty well connected.Notably, Ramsey and another younger cast member, Sebastian Croft, both starred in season six of Game of Thrones.Ramsey also worked with James Blunt on the film Sunny Dancer, was interviewed by James Acaster on his Off Menu podcast - and had a funny chat about their "vegan-ish" diet with Romesh Ranganathan on The Jonathan Ross Show.Ahead of the show, Croft said he didn't know many people aside from Ramsey before joining."One of the other things I'm excited about is this will be the first time I'm playing with people who, on the whole, don't know me and don't know how I work,” he said.Richard and Jerry go way back“I just don't believe Richard's a traitor. I've known him 30 years and he's my neighbour.”That was American model Jerry Hall, speaking after actor Richard E Grant came under (admittedly self-inflicted) pressure in the opening episode of the series.As well as being neighbours, the pair are linked in lots of other ways.Image source, Rune Hellestad/Corbis via Getty ImagesImage caption, The pair pictured together at the Chelsea Flower Show in 2003Grant was pictured leaving Hall's wedding to Rupert Murdoch in 2016; in 2003, they were pictured together at Chelsea Flower Show, and they also acted in children's film Tooth back in 2004."It was ridiculous,"Jerry said of the film. "We had such a laugh, and I went on holiday with him earlier this year, just after Christmas to Africa with some friends. And we danced all night. We had so much fun! Little did we know back then that we'd both be here [on Celebrity Traitors]."Now they've taken the next step and moved in together, will they be arguing over who takes the bins out? We are here for it.Romesh and Julie connected by The Weakest LinkYes, you know Romesh Ranganathan is the host of The Weakest Link.But did you know actor Julie Hesmondhalgh is the voiceover narrator for the quiz show?Here are a few other connections you may not have known about.Hesmondhalgh and Michael Sheen both fronted Papyrus's online child safety campaign back in 2020.YouTuber King Kenny was one of 10 online stars competing in the game show Would You Rather, hosted by Romesh Ranganathan.And singers James Blunt and Leigh-Anne Pinnock are both Brit Award winners. Both being successful musicians, it wouldn't be surprising if they have mingled together at events over the years.Where does this leave those with fewer friends?While some of the celebrities have known each other for 30 years, others have no friends in the castle at all.My Mad Fat Diary actor Sharon Rooney and Industry star Myha'la, for instance, have fewer connections than the others.And that can be a disadvantage. Remember Niko Omilana and Ruth Codd last year?After they were banished early on, a theory spread on social media that they were voted out because the other celebrities didn't know them that well.But it can definitely go both ways.Leigh-Anne Pinnock has said the fact she doesn't know many people might actually help her."I think I'm at a slight advantage because people just know me as Leigh-Anne from Little Mix, and they don't really know my personality that well," she said.What's clear is that these prior connections are "exactly the sort of thing" that makes Celebrity Traitors so fascinating, as TV reporter Siobhan Synnot told me.But - like Pinnock - she agrees that having loads of friends doesn't necessarily end up helping you."Quite often in The Traitors," she says, "that familiarity becomes a disadvantage".Players, you have been warned.When is The Celebrity Traitors next on TV?There are new episodes of The Celebrity Traitors every Thursday and Friday. The next episode is this Thursday 8 October at 8pm on BBC One and iPlayer, with another at the same time on Friday 9 October.The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked is next on this Thursday 8 October at 9.05pm on BBC One and iPlayer.

schema.headline: The Celebrity Traitors connections that might surprise you, from Jerry Hall and Richard E Grant to Rob and Romesh

title: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed
description: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on
body: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on bail.The 25-year-old man was arrested in the London borough of Westminster on Thursday. Searches of two properties in the same area have now finished. A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire last weekend.Five other men in their twenties were arrested and were subsequently released on police bail. All five were UK nationals from London.The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the events are continuing, police said.Last weekend, the five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF), sparking a major security incident.The BBC understands that one of the men had dialled 999 himself, about an hour before a local farmer alerted police to a "large group" of masked men near the vehicles.They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail on Monday in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting that afternoon in response. He later said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident, but did not provide any more details.Tehran has strongly denied any involvement. The Iranian embassy in London said on Monday that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".Late on Monday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a TV show that it was clear a "foreign actor" had been involved in events over the weekend.Without providing evidence or giving further details, he told Fox News network's "Hannity" programme: "What happened, what almost happened, what could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation. It's one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor."Speaking earlier at the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump said he would not have let the five men arrested out on bail, and that he was "surprised" they had been released."We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.

schema.headline: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed

title: Protesters across Spain demand action over housing crisis
description: One of the biggest demonstration happened in the capital, Madrid, where estimates of the number of participants varied widely. The city's Tenants' Uni
body: One of the biggest demonstration happened in the capital, Madrid, where estimates of the number of participants varied widely. The city's Tenants' Union said there were 500,000, while officials put the figure at 70,000.Demonstrators held banners reading "There won't be peace for rentism" and "I study to have a future, not to have a tiny apartment". They shook the keys they were holding and chanted: "We have the keys of all the city".Some had also camped in one of the city's main squares, Puerta del Sol, for days.One protester, David, told RTVE ahead of the protest: "We're not here for pleasure or comfort. We're here out of conviction."Another protester, 26-year-old librarian Marcos Sainz, told AFP news agency that he used to share a two-bedroom flat with friends, paying 900 euros (£766) a month in rent. Today, he said a one-bedroom flat often costs 1,000 euros.Sainz said he would protest against rent rises "until someone dares to regulate it all", or "we'll all have to leave Madrid".On Friday night, Madrid's Tenants' Union said that although the government's proposed measures were insufficient, the rejection of the proposed legislation "exacerbates the housing crisis which is costing the working class their lives".It is calling for a general strike over the housing crisis.The legislation put forward in Congress on Friday was divided into two decrees.The first included the suspension of evictions of vulnerable tenants until 2030, a two-year extension to rental leases due to expire before 2028, tax increases for tourist apartments, and a restriction on the purchase of residential properties by  so-called "vulture funds".The second decree included the automatic renewal of rental contracts, a major demand of many on the left and the Tenants' Union.MPs rejected the first decree by 178 votes to 172 and voted against the second by 184 to 166.Prior to the vote, the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox had already said they would vote against both initiatives, leaving the minority government depending on the support of smaller nationalist parties in Catalonia and the Basque Country.However, by the eve of the parliamentary session, the centre-right, pro-independence Together for Catalonia (JxCat) had signalled its opposition to both laws, condemning them to failure.Sánchez's ruling coalition hurriedly drew up the decree laws in an effort to defuse the housing protests that were sparked when 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted in September.The social backlash led to the company that owns Abascal's flat, Urbagestión, negotiating her return to the flat on a low rent. However, protests have continued.

schema.headline: Protesters across Spain demand action over housing crisis

title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026: Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1
description: Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Ba
body: Even Lewis Hamilton, starting from his equal best grid position of the year in second place, fears Max Verstappen will be tough to beat in Sunday's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.Verstappen has dominated the weekend so far on Formula 1's return to the Sepang track for the first time since 2017.Hamilton joins him on the front row to revive memories of their no-holds-barred title battle five years ago.But at nearly 0.3 seconds slower in qualifying, and with the pace Verstappen has shown all weekend, Hamilton's mindset on Saturday was to "just try my best to hold on to him tomorrow".This was Verstappen's first pole position of the year - a remarkable statistic for someone who came within two points of winning a fifth world title last year after one of the all-time great fightbacks.Red Bull started the year off the pace - the car was on average more than 0.5secs a lap slower than Mercedes in the first half of the year - and for a time there were questions as to whether Verstappen would stick around for 2027.But after being courted by McLaren, Verstappen signed a two-year contract extension over the summer break, saying he believed in the Red Bull project and didn't mind putting in the work to turn things around. Verstappen arrived in Malaysia after a run of three consecutive podium finishes, and with Red Bull hoping to prove out an upgrade that had seen them finish less than 0.2secs off victory in Baku last Sunday.In the tropical heat of Malaysia, around the demanding long corners of this track with perhaps the roughest surface of the season, the upgrade - centred on a new floor - has more than proved its worth."It's been an incredible result for us," Verstappen said. "Looking at the season, how it started for us and the progression that we have made. At some tracks we were kind of close, but now I think this weekend it was very positive for us."We have been adding bits to the car and they have worked. It's simple as that. When they work, you gain lap time, you have a better overall balance in the car."So with tyres that are very sensitive to balance, that gives you also more lap time."And then on a track probably where it's all very hot and you want a, let's say, stable balance or connected balance, then that's very important. And that's what we have found a little bit more over the last weekends."Hamilton, for one, but also Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who under-performed slightly in qualifying because of a combination between an unusual tyre strategy and an error on an early run.The world championship leader's fourth place becomes third on the grid with Hadjar's penalty, and he can usually be relied upon to be a factor in the race.Antonelli's main focus will be his advantage over team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points and starts four places behind, his momentum from his Baku win stalled, and somewhat perplexed as to his and his team's lack of pace.At Mercedes, the bigger question is over the aerodynamic upgrade they brought to the car this weekend.Mercedes are lagging behind their rivals when it comes to developing their car this season, apparently at least in part because they front-loaded their spend early in the season.But this first big update since the Canadian Grand Prix in June has not yet proved the step they had expected.The question is whether that is to do with the parts themselves or the very specific conditions of this weekend, in the heat and on the rough track surface, which is putting the tyres through the mill, and massively limiting the useful laps teams can do in terms of set-up work.Antonelli said: "With this new package, obviously the window of the way the car operates is different. So, we're trying to understand in which window the car performance is best, in the high-speed corner and low-speed corners."Our high-speed performance has been very strong this weekend. We were very quick in the high-speed, but in the low-speed we lacked. So, we need to understand why and try to move on and improve."As for the race, Antonelli said: "Track position is going to be very important. Strategy is going to be really important."It's a race where we will attack. Because undercut (stopping first and gaining time on a rival on fresh tyres) is incredibly powerful."So whenever there's an opportunity, we should go for maybe an undercut and try to maximise our opportunity."Tomorrow might be two stops, three stops. We don't know. But the only thing we know is that it's going to be roasting hot out there."

schema.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026: Red Bull upgrade enlivens F1

title: The Prem: Newcastle 19-24 Leicester - Tigers pick up first win of season.
description: The PremNewcastle (5) 19Tries: Ene, McGuigan, Jordan Cons: Connon, HenryLeicester (17) 24Tries: Moli, Radwan, Hurd Cons: Searle 3 Pens: SearleLeiceste
body: The PremNewcastle (5) 19Tries: Ene, McGuigan, Jordan Cons: Connon, HenryLeicester (17) 24Tries: Moli, Radwan, Hurd Cons: Searle 3 Pens: SearleLeicester Tigers picked up their first win of the season with a tense and hard-fought victory at Newcastle Red Bulls.Former Newcastle winger Adam Radwan scored on his return to Kingston Park as the Tigers won for the first time in seven matches in all competitions, following a dismal run which stretches back into last season.After being edged out by two points in a high-scoring thriller by Saracens six days ago, Leicester had to show their grit and determination to cling on to victory against a Newcastle side who threatened a late comeback.Newcastle took the lead through Obi Ene's early score but, despite putting in a positive showing, they ultimately came up just short in their first home match of the season.Ene scored three minutes into his Prem debut after Newcastle moved the ball left. The former Sale winger weaved inside, having collected fly-half Brett Connon's excellent cut-out pass, to dive over for the opener.But Leicester hit back when hooker Samiuela Moli launched himself over at the back of a driving maul and Billy Searle popped over the conversion to give Tigers a slender advantage.Gabriel Hamer-Webb had an opportunity to go over for Leicester soon after but was pushed into touch by an excellent try-saving tackle from Christian Wade, before Hamer-Webb made his own outstanding score-stopping challenge as Newcastle's Harrison Obatoyinbo threatened to break clear.That moment proved to be pivotal as former Newcastle winger Radwan latched on to Freddie Steward's exquisite grubber kick to touch down. After Searle kicked the conversion, the fly-half then added a penalty in front of the sticks.Newcastle missed two presentable opportunities to score a second try before half-time and the match restarted in a scrappy manner after the break - until Ene was prevented from scoring a second try of the match thanks to a textbook challenge from Leicester replacement Will Wand.Radwan spurned a good opportunity to score his second, kicking the ball dead when he had a whole half of the field to run into. Leicester were made to pay for their profligacy when George McGuigan's pick-and-go enabled him to drive over from close range to help pull the deficit back to five points.Leicester got a vital third try of the night when Will Hurd's quick tap let him barrel over, and Searle kicked the conversion to make it a two-score game once more with 12 minutes remaining.Newcastle carved through Leicester with just under seven minutes left when Ollie Leatherbarrow's bold carry saw him break a tackle as Cameron Jordan went over with Zack Henry adding the extras.With the clock ticking down, Wade carried Newcastle forward with a trademark burst down the wing, but the home side were eventually guilty of holding on as Leicester gratefully kicked to touch to claim victory.Newcastle Red Bulls director of rugby Dan McFarland told BBC Radio Newcastle:"I'm really disappointed, to be honest. It was a game we could have won. Really pleased with the way we approached the game. I thought we were full of effort, full of energy."Most importantly, we were full of the endeavour that we wanted to put in, in terms of the way we wanted to play the game."Unfortunately, we were not accurate enough in key areas - but that will grow."We are trying not to play in a boring way. Today, we weren't where we wanted to be. In the first half, we gave away penalties at set-piece and let them into our 22. I thought we improved in that area as the game went on."Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling told BBC Radio Leicester:"Gritty and dogged. Defensively, some good resolve and they're [Newcastle] going to break some teams this year with their quality attack and good speed."You go all pre-season and you try to build some real cohesion and you lose a lot of guys in the same position, but no excuses, we've just got to be better. I've got to help those guys to be able to execute in those moments."There's loads to improve on. The general feeling in the changing room is disappointment, which is great for me."Accuracy in the second half, especially at set-piece, we didn't allow ourselves to build up some pressure."Newcastle Red Bulls: Obatoyinbo; Wade, Hearle, Harris, Ene; Connon, Elliott; Rakete-Stones, McGuigan, Millar Mills; Usher, Jordan, Hicks, Christie (capt), Sotutu.Replacements: Fletcher, Brocklebank, Harper, Molina, Leatherbarrow, Graham, Benitez Cruz, Henry.Leicester Tigers: Steward; Radwan, Kata, Bailey, Hamer-Webb; Searle, Van Poortvliet (capt); Vunipola, Moli, Heyes; Thompson, Henderson, Wainwright, Reffell, Cracknell.Replacements: Thunder, Haffar, Hurd, Manz, Moro, Whiteley, Wand, Hassell-Collins.Referee: Christophe Ridley.

title: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final
description: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challengeImage source, Richard Sellers/PAImage caption, Kevin Sinfield carried the Super League Grand Final tro
body: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challengeImage source, Richard Sellers/PAImage caption, Kevin Sinfield carried the Super League Grand Final trophy into Old Trafford after completing the challengeByGrace WoodYorkshireSir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way.The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.Image source, PA MediaImage caption, Prince William and Catherine made an unexpected appearance in Wakefield on Tuesday to meet Sir KevinAlong the way he was surprised by royals, including The Prince and Princess of Wales and the Princess Royal, as well as famous names from the sporting world such as former England football manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Leeds boxer Josh Warrington.Each day was split into 7km, hour-long blocks with an additional extra mile for members of the MND community to join.Funds raised by the challenge will go towards the work of the MND Association, Leeds Hospitals Charity, My Name5 Doddie Foundation, Darby Rimmer Foundation, MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association.Image source, Mike Egerton/PAImage caption, Sinfield arrived at Old Trafford at about 17:00 BSTSinfield, 45, who played his entire professional career with Leeds Rhinos, is one of the most successful players in Super League history.He and Burrow met at the Leeds Rhinos academy aged 14 and 12. They went on to win seven titles together with Leeds Rhinos.Burrow's wife, Lindsey Burrow, told BBC Radio 4's PM that her late husband "would have been incredibly proud" of his friend."It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community," Lindsey said."It's just incredible. I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years," she added.Sinfield's son, Jack Sinfield, lined up in the Wakefield side seeking to clinch their first top-flight title since 1968.Get in touchYour Voice

title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it
description: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the mo
body: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the money to get there is a marathon.The "Your First Home" scheme, announced on Saturday, aims to help first-time buyers in England get on the housing ladder with a small deposit.Currently a 5% deposit on the average UK house price of £272,000 plus moving costs and legal fees - will set you back about £16,850, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.That's daunting, but here are four ways that experts say you can at least make a start on saving for a deposit.1. Make saving like a billDepositing an amount you can afford into a regular savers account the day after you are paid is a good way to start, suggests Anna Bowes, savings expert at financial advisers The Private Office."It becomes like another bill, but one that you can benefit from in the future," she says.The type of account that's suitable depends on your circumstances.Some of the ones that pay the highest interest  are only accessible if you hold a current account with the provider, she says.Other considerations are whether you can lock the money away for longer, to receive a better savings rate.If you don't have a buffer of other savings, then experts say an easy access account gives you the chance to dip into the money to pay an unexpected bill.2. You could get £1,000 a year You can save up to £4,000 a year in a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (LISA) and the government guarantees a 25% bonus. So, if you put the full amount in then the government will add £1,000 a year. But there is a catch, that has left some people out of pocket. Money saved in a LISA can only be used to buy a first home up to the value of £450,000 - a threshold that has not changed since 2017. The only other time you can withdraw the money is after the age of 60 or in the exceptional case that you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.Withdrawal under any other circumstances means you get hit with a penalty - so you could get back less than you put in.Ministers are planning to replace the LISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, but there are no clear details yet about how it will work.3. Start earlyThe earlier you start saving the more you can build up thanks to the magic of compound interest. In short, interest is added on a larger and larger pot as time goes by.Bowes says that saving £50 a month from the age of 20 would give you about £41,000 in 30 years' time when you hit 50, assuming interest of 5% is paid a year.Start 10 years later, and you'd need to save more than double - £101 a month - to have the same amount at the age of 50.Investing in stocks and shares is another option, but the value of investments can go down as well as up.4. Save lessAn increasing number of lenders are offering mortgage deals with little or no deposit required.David Hollingworth, from L&C, points to mortgages that have deposits starting from £5,000 and allow people to borrow up to 98% or 99% of the property purchase price.They might not always be the best option, and not everyone will be eligible.And, of course, some first-time buyers turn to their parents for help. Again that's not available to all, but a survey by the Nationwide Building Society suggests that more than half of parents who charge their adult children rent are putting some or all of the money towards helping their child save to buy their own home.Get in touchAre you trying to get on to the property ladder? Share your experience. Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

title: Why Canada is preparing for a (longshot) US invasion
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion.Noting the risk was low and the lik
body: Prime Minister Mark Carney admitted last week that he has prepared for a once-unthinkable scenario - a US invasion.Noting the risk was low and the likelihood highly improbable, he told the New York Times he had a responsibility to consider all possibilities as the US-Canada relationship is redefined under the Donald Trump presidency."That's just risk management," Carney said.Trump's global tariffs and his often-repeated desire to make Canada the 51st state has led Canada to war game an attack by the Americans.In 2025, the US president said it was "highly unlikely" that the US would ever use force against Canada. Instead he said, he would continue to exert economic pressures to obtain political aims."President Trump has done more than anyone to protect the great people of Canada," the White House told the BBC in a statement this week.Military experts who spoke to the BBC also think an invasion is a long shot, pointing to the multiple ways the two countries work together on defence.But the issue is clearly weighing on Canadians' minds.In January, after the US captured Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela, a Leger poll suggested that over 30% of Canadians believed that a US invasion was likely.A war between Canada and the US would be complicated and almost difficult to imagine, said Lt-Gen Christopher Coates, a former military officer of 34 years with the Royal Canadian Air Force who held various senior positions."I was involved in military operations for my whole career, and we never considered the possibility that there would be a military attack coming from US territory," he told the BBC.Coates, who had served on Nato missions, noted that Canada and the US collaborate on many aspects of military defence.They are both members of the north Atlantic defence alliance, which mandates members to defend a fellow member-nation should they be attacked.The two countries also conduct joint Arctic defence missions under the North American Aerospace Defence Command (NORAD), and frequently share intelligence.Because of this, Coates said he believes an attack by the US on Canada would not begin with an armed assault, but rather with more discreet means like cyberwarfare.After World War II, Canada and the US became natural allies for the latter part of the 20th Century, and have become heavily integrated economically, militarily and culturally.But it wasn't always this way. In fact, a core tenet of Canada's identity is its resistance of US expansionism in the 18th and 19th Centuries, said Tim Foran, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum."Fear of the United States is foundational to the political project that is Canada," he said.Canada was formed as a collection of British North American colonies who remained loyal to the British Crown when the colonies in the modern-day US rebelled.Before the formation of Canada, the US had attempted to invade British North American colonies, taking control of Montreal in 1775 and nearly conquering Quebec City.In the war of 1812, the Americans invaded what was known then as Upper Canada, Lower Canada and the maritime colonies repeatedly, resulting in a stalemate. During that war, British troops famously burned down the White House in retaliation.Foran said that at the time, the colonies that later became Canada relied on Great Britain and its Royal Navy for its defence, as well as indigenous peoples who served as generals in major battles.Canada again contemplated war with the US post-World War I in response to its growing power and influence.It drafted a plan that was informed by secret trips to border cities made by Canadian army generals, who would pose as tourists and snap photos of bridges and highways for intelligence.They also spoke to local residents to better understand their enemy.A war was an unlikely scenario then, said Andrew Burtch, a researcher with the Canadian War Museum with expertise on Canada in the 20th Century, but the Canadians still wanted to be prepared."That's part of what militaries do," he said. "They envisage all sorts of different scenarios."Even if a US invasion is extremely unlikely, Matthew Schmidt, an associate professor of national security at the University of New Haven in Connecticut, said the fact that Canadians were preparing was a sign of just how drastically the global order has shifted.He added Canadian leaders do have hard questions to ask about how closely they want to continue working with the American military - a partnership that gives them valuable information should they want to harm Canada in any way."It's really doing harm to relationships with the United States, and there's a certain amount of legitimate fear," he said.Americans might not take Trump's comments about making Canada the 51st state seriously, he said, but Canadians clearly do - and are prepared to defend themselves if needed.So what would it be like if it happened?The first phase of a war could be quite short.According to the model used by the Canadian military, as reported on by the Globe and Mail newspaper earlier this year, a US attack would see Canada's strategic positions overwhelmed within a weekIts military would quickly be outnumbered, forcing Canadian forces to resort to guerilla-type warfare to try to suppress their enemy.Allied nations like France and Britain would be called on to provide support and defence for Canada, the newspaper reported in January, citing senior government officials.The theoretical model is believed to be the first time in a century that Canada planned for an American assault.The modelling is on the lighter end of military combat planning, Coates said.He said that Canada, unlike its Nato allies, was lagging behind when it came to having a response plan in place in the event of any ground invasion, and that it was now playing catch-up in this era of unpredictable geopolitics.Part of that, he said, was made evident by a recent call by Canada's defence chief to drastically increase the size of its military, including the addition of as many as 300,000 lightly trained citizen soldiers.An invasion of Canada might not be straightforward from the US point of view either.Even with its outsized military, the US would have a difficult time getting buy-in for a fight with Canada, said Schmidt."I think you would have a large number of American officers who would resign if given the order to invade Canada," he said."They would see it as an illegal and immoral order."Schmidt said Canadian soldiers and American soldiers routinely train together, and share a mutual respect.But in the unlikely scenario that relations would deteriorate to the point of combat, Schmidt said the US would likely focus on acquiring valuable Canadian resources like oil and minerals, and political decapitation."You would see a a kind of operation that would mirror perhaps what you saw in Venezuela," he said, referring to US military action earlier this year to capture former Venezuelan President Maduro.Although he acknowledged the US has greater military capacity, he said that "pound for pound" Canadian soldiers would be able to put up a fight.

schema.headline: Why Canada is preparing for a (longshot) US invasion

title: Newcastle friends embark on 20-year board game battle
description: Image source, War With A MateImage caption, James Purcell and Andy Taeger will officially start Campaign for North Africa on 30 OctoberByEvie LakeNort
body: Image source, War With A MateImage caption, James Purcell and Andy Taeger will officially start Campaign for North Africa on 30 OctoberByEvie LakeNorth East and CumbriaTwo friends from Newcastle have set themselves the challenge of completing a board game which has never officially been completed. They expect it will take 20 years as they battle to fit it around their everyday lives - but while games can often put friendships to the test, the pair are determined to see it through, no matter how different life will look.What would you be willing to commit 1,500 hours of your life doing?Playing a game about a week during World War Two in North Africa might not be top of your list - but James Purcell, 29, and Andy Taeger, 30, decided to do just that.The pair met about a decade ago at a house party and became fast friends after duetting to a James Blunt song.They have spent every week since playing Dungeons and Dragons together."One day we were playing and this friend just mentioned off-handedly that there was a game that supposedly had never been finished and takes up to 1,500 hours," Purcell says."We had a bit of a laugh about it, thought nothing of it, and then a few weeks later we were at the pub and one of us said 'have you been thinking about that board game a lot?'"They spent the next few hours in the pub discussing it and left committed to playing Campaign for North Africa in its entirety.18-month drawThat was in October 2024. And for Purcell and Taeger, there's no going back.The strategic board wargame was released in 1978 and simulates the entire North African campaign of World War Two. Purcell says there has been no evidenced play of the full game and theirs would be the first occasion."The game was never fully playtested by the designers either," he adds.Now two years on from their original commitment, the pair have managed a six-turn practice run to get to grips with the rules before jumping into the full game, which is 111 turns.Every turn simulates a real week during World War Two in North Africa. Purcell is playing as the Axis forces - Germany, Italy, Japan - while Taeger is playing as the Commonwealth.While 10 players are suggested, they are making do with just two.Through spreadsheets they have to keep track of things like ammunition, food, fuel, water, even down to the rate at which water evaporates depending on the heat.Image source, War With A MateImage caption, A practice run took more than a year to completeThe practice ended in a draw and took 18 months to complete alongside their jobs and everyday lives.Purcell works in mental health services while Taeger is a software developer."It feels sometimes like a job as well, we're filling out spreadsheets more so than playing a game, so a lot of the time it doesn't feel like fun, it feels like admin," Purcell says.To hold themselves accountable, they set up a podcast, War With A Mate, which has already had more than 90 episodes.And it has a good following already, with Purcell joking it is nice not having to bribe his friends and family to listen along.Finding common groundBut board games are known to get tense, even more so if you are at war with one another, and the friends are mindful of that."We're trying to keep it fairly chill, but sometimes it'll come down to a single dice roll and someone gets unlucky and there has been a bit of, not quite throwing pieces around because the board's too big, but there have been moments of frustration and tension," Taeger says.Purcell adds: "I've had a few hissy fits, just with the rules being so complicated."I've been a bit annoyed when we've been so far in and I've realised I've done something wrong and had to make new plans based on that."Because to finish a single turn, it takes us months at a time."But their podcast has a segment called Common Ground which forces the pair to try and agree on something from the episode, no matter how ridiculous.They are hopeful it will stop them fighting.'20-year void'The friends are now gearing up to starting their official Campaign for North Africa on 30 October, which will coincide with the podcast's 100th episode."I think when we start the full game, it'll be exciting," Purcell says."And then from there we've got the sort of void of 20 plus years that it'll take to finish the game."So I'm kind of worried that the excitement might wear off and then we're just locked into this thing for two decades."War With A Mate already has listeners from around the globe, many of whom are happy they get to experience the game without having to do hundreds of hours of legwork."I think at certain times it'll be our biggest regret starting it and sometimes it'll be some real highs," Taeger says."But I think it'll be part people listening along to our deteriorating mental state."It is certain the pair's lives will look different after 20 years, when they hope to have completed the game.Purcell says: "It's sort of weird knowing that we'll be 20 years older."We can have any sort of different living circumstance, careers, so it's strange that this game is going to be a constant through that and it already has for two years."So it'll be interesting to see how it maps across."Follow BBC Newcastle on X, external, Facebook, external, Nextdoor and Instagram, external and listen to Radio Newcastle on BBC Sounds.Get in touchDo you have a story suggestion for BBC Tyne?

schema.headline: Newcastle friends embark on 20-year board game battle

title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
description: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill
body: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence."Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said. Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.Attorneys for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now"."What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings. She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator. The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

schema.headline: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
